description: Pinned evaluation toolchain. Any change to these versions invalidates cross-run comparability and must be recorded in the result snapshot.

runner.name: harbor
notes: Harbor owns task, agent, environment, trial, and verifier execution.
Stable releases only. Harbor publishes daily 0.x.y.devYYYYMMDDHHMM builds which must not be used for published results.
Harbor default environment type. Daytona is the planned first hosted backend.
Host CLI now matches the pin. terminal-bench-glm53-smoke reported codex 0.151.0 from inside the sandbox.

Harbor's codex agent overrides only `openai_base_url` and leaves the built-in `openai` provider active. That provider has websockets enabled, so codex dials wss://<base>/responses, which Merge Gateway answers 403. Reproduced on 2026-09-02 with a bare `openai_base_url` config: 8 failed connects, 5 reconnects, then HTTPS fallback on every trial. Declaring a custom `[model_providers.merge-gateway]` with `supports_websockets = false` removes it (0 attempts, 0 403s, first-try HTTPS). Supplied per agent via `kwargs.config` in the job yaml; a top-level `config:` key is silently dropped.

Host CLI is one patch ahead of the pin. terminal-bench-glm53-smoke reported claude-code 2.1.252 from inside the sandbox, so the published rows are 2.1.252, not the pinned 2.1.251. Either move the pin or reinstall 2.1.251 before the full 2x2.
`opencode --version` returns empty output on the current machine, so the installed CLI version cannot be verified.
~/.opencode/package.json only declares @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.4, which is the plugin and not the CLI.
Installed as the bun dependency @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent; node_modules is absent until `bun install` runs.
Never committed. Materialized into the gitignored .env.local for Harbor --env-file runs.

vendorPinning.why: The gateway picks the serving vendor unless the request body names one, and the default is not the fastest: on zai/glm-5.3-flash, unpinned traffic went to zai at ~36 tok/s while particle served the same model at ~184 tok/s for the same price. Vendor is therefore part of the eval specification, not an implementation detail.
vendorPinning.whyProxy: The pin is only accepted as a JSON body field (`vendor`); `x-merge-vendor` and `x-vendor` headers were probed and silently dropped. Neither Codex nor Claude Code can inject a body field, so a reverse proxy inserts it.
vendorPinning.validation: Every pin checked against the live catalog, then probed on /v1/openai/responses through the proxy: all six returned HTTP 200 with status=completed and an x-merge-vendor matching the pin.
vendorPinning.containerReachability: Containers reach the host proxy at http://host.docker.internal:8787 with no extra host mapping on Docker Desktop; verified 2026-09-02.
vendorPinning.provenance: The proxy pins the vendor but leaves no trace in Harbor's output, so each agent also sets HEVAL_VENDOR to the vendor its model is pinned to. harbor/report/trials.ts reads it into TrialRow.vendor; without it routeFor() refuses to guess a rate card and every Codex row drops out of the cost chart. The yaml's HEVAL_VENDOR values are checked against pins.json - they are two copies of one fact and must not drift.
vendorPinning.smokeVerified: 2026-09-02, jobs/composio-mirror-smoke: 1/1 trials, reward 1.0, 2m29s. 19 proxy requests all HTTP 200 with served vendor == pinned vendor on every one, and 0 websocket/403/reconnect lines in the in-container codex log.

control.role: Baseline held constant; same dated model as the published smoke snapshot.

caveats: Reasoning model: spends output budget on thinking before emitting content. Under a tight max-token cap it returns empty content with a `reasoning_exhausted` warning, which grades as a task failure and misreads as weak model performance.

Gateway lists four vendors at a 10x price spread (particle/zai $0.015/$0.05 per Mtok; wafer/baseten $0.15/$0.50). Vendor is not pinned, so it is an uncontrolled variable that must appear in snapshot limitations.

composioMirrorSweep.source: https://x.com/composio/status/2092983288423927939 (2026-08-27): 5 open-weight models on 30 multi-step agentic tasks.
composioMirrorSweep.note: Composio's tasks were their own SaaS tool-calling scenarios, not Terminal-Bench. The model lineup and comparison shape transfer; the absolute scores do not.
